long_biography.plain_text:
Richard Saker entered a grocery tradition rooted in his great-grandfather's Freehold store and his father's early membership in the Wakefern cooperative. As chairman, president and chief executive, he expanded the family operation while retaining local ownership and cooperative purchasing. A family-led transaction also returned predecessor Foodarama to private ownership.

The business added large replacement stores and acquired seven Perlmart ShopRites, bringing its current network to 40 supermarkets and nearly 12,000 employees. Saker also continued the family's trade-association involvement by chairing the New Jersey Food Council. The company's community programme supports food banks, hunger-relief campaigns and organisations serving people with ALS across its central and coastal New Jersey markets.
